newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close higher on crop worries.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close higher on crop worries.

text.p: CBOT soy products closed higher, led by soybeans on ideas a drought in South America would cut production, forcing an increase in U.S. exports, traders said.

Weather Services Corp on Monday said dry weather in some major soybean areas of Argentina continued to stress the developing crop. Frost and freezing temperatures over the weekend could lead to quality losses and possible yield losses, WSC said.
The U.S. agricultural attache cut Argentina's soybean output estimate to 13.25 million tonnes from 13.50 million.
Floor sources also cited rumors a leading U.S. analytical firm had cut its estimate for Argentina's soybean production due to the drought late in the growing season.
Soy products drew strength from USDA's weekly export inspections data. USDA on Monday put weekly export inspections at 13.8 million bushels.
The figure suggested the export pace was outstripping USDA's expectations, traders said.
Soymeal closed $5.90 to $1.30 per ton higher with May up $5.90 at $287.40. Soyoil ended 0.32 to 0.27 cent per lb higher with May up 0.29 at 24.16 cents.
USDA on March 11 pegged 1996-97 U.S. soybean exports at 900 million bushels. Analysts said export inspections needed to drop below 10 million bushels per week to meet USDA's target.

Gains were limited by speculation that a cold, wet spring in the U.S. Midwest would force farmers to switch intended corn acreage to soybeans. Soybeans can be planted as late as July while corn must be in the ground by June.
On the day, ADM bought 300 lots May soymeal and 200 lots July, Cargill bought 200 May and 250 July, traders said.
E.D. and F. Man International bought 300 lots July and Merrill Lynch and Lehman Brothers each bought 300 lots May.
In soyoil, ADM bought 300 lots May and Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought 300 July and 400 May, pit sources said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 27,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 33,863 lots. Soyoil volume was estimated at 20,000 lots, against Friday's actual of 24,352 lots.
